pr_body:
shell_fprintf() can cause deadlock if called before the shell thread is running.  shell_start() can cause deadlock because it uses shell_fprintf().

shell_uninit() uses a kill signal to shutdown the shell thread.  However, the kill signal does not work when the thread is not polling the signal.

This commit used the wr_mtx mutex to lock when starting the shell thread.  shell_fprintf() checks that the shell is not in the unitialized or initialized state before running.  The shell_uninit() kill mechanism was reworked.

Fixes #24293.  
Might fix #14520 as well.

review_comments: can you move this lock to `shell_internal_fprintf` function? I noticed that internal fprintf is actually not protected so if `shell_fprintf` is called from other context than shell command there is a chance that it will clash.
That is likely a better place for the lock.  I will have a look at that tomorrow.
@nordic-krch I had a closer look and it appears that shell_fprintf() and shell_internal_fprintf() both call shell_internal_vfprintf().

All of the printf's appear to converge to shell_fprintf_fmt() in shell_fprintf.c.  We do not have the same mutex here because we do not have the shell struct passed down to here.  So, we would need to create another one in the shell_fprintf struct and initialize it in instance_init().  Do you see any problems with that?
No, cannot put it there ... that is a const struct.

ok, i think that your initial proposal is actually ok.

Whole shell processing is done under mutex lock:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ef4d62749c9688e60206a9cbc299dcacf0f59767/subsys/shell/shell.c#L1189

It is unlocked only when user command handler is called to allow printing from that context. If `shell_print` is called from another context then this mutex will protect access. What is not protected is the start portion and your current patch is adding it.

@nordic-krch 
Function `shell_internal_fprintf` is not protected by the lock on purpose. Please do not lock it :)
@jakub-uC agree, my initial proposal was wrong. However, shell start shall be locked.

@jakub-uC Is it possible that not protecting shell_fprintf_fmt() can cause a problem because of shell_pend_on_txdone()?  When I was debugging this issue I encountered problems when shell_pend_on_txdone() waits for an event that never happens.  One example of this is encountered when starting the shell.  I have noticed other situations where shell_pend_on_txdone() pends forever when done out of order
